regime_context: The detector shows a broad but non-directional leadership rotation (9 of 16 themes eligible; absorption 0.31) with precious metals — Silver & Royalties and Gold Miners — holding the top two momentum ranks, while Big Banks and Insurers are the only 'trend' Hurst-tagged non-energy financials. The validated edge here is risk control (gate_helps true), not prediction; the macro backdrop is geopolitical-noise-dominant (98% unscheduled share), so I keep conviction low and lean mostly on the risk-control leg.
emerging_watch: Big Banks (ZEB.TO) is the only non-insurer financial with a 'trend' Hurst tag and eligible=true; the watch condition is a confirmed broadening of rotation breadth (breadth_of_rotation.frac rising above 0.6) accompanied by Big Banks' score staying positive and its durability_bar crossing above 0.65 — without either of those, the watch retires.

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Top momentum rank (2.11), eligible under the absolute-trend gate, durability_bar 0.7, breadth 1.0, and not crowded (z=0.94) — so the trend-following/vol-aware logic permits exposure without a crowding cap. This is a focus-lens call only, not a return forecast; the gate is the only validated staying-power leg.
theses.dissent: Hurst tag is 'mixed', not 'trend'; silver has a history of violent two-sided swings, and the macro backdrop (geopolitical noise, 98% unscheduled) can spike real rates against precious metals abruptly, crushing the trade faster than the gate can de-risk.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO falls below its 20-day simple moving average while Gold Miners (XGD.TO) also turns negative over the same horizon before the check-by date.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Rank 2 (1.973), eligible, durability_bar 0.75 (highest among top three), breadth 1.0, not crowded (z=0.73). Coins with the leader on theme and proxy, so the same gate-logic applies; the higher durability_bar slightly favors holding power in a pullback.
theses.dissent: Same proxy (XGD.TO) means this is not diversified away from Silver & Royalties; if the precious-metals narrative is attention-driven rather than flow-driven, both names mean-revert together and the 'mixed' Hurst tag offers no trend persistence.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO loses its eligibility under the absolute-trend gate before the check-by date.

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Rank 3 (1.678) and eligible, but crowded=true (z=1.23). Per guardrails this is a sizing caution, not a fade; as a directional lean we express it as underweight relative to the precious-metals exposure, not as a short — reflexivity risk on the crowded leader-adjacent name.
theses.dissent: Copper is a genuine inflation/geopolitics hedge now (macro themes: inflation, geopolitics); crowding here may reflect real defensive demand, and underweighting a high-rank eligible theme can lag if the gate keeps it open.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO maintains eligibility under the absolute-trend gate for more than one month while crowding_z stays above 1.0 and the price keeps making new highs.

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
